answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each identity to one carrier-verified phone number, re-verified every epoch: you cannot forge a carrier record, and a shared registry lets one number back only one identity. A farm wanting 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 distinct numbers at about $8 each: $8,000 per epoch, a river of recurring fees. The named failure is the SIM-farm sweep: carrier velocity checks flag over three weekly activations per device, and one flagged number voids every identity tied to that device, so a farm chasing cheap nectar in throwaway numbers loses all its fakes at once.
